chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from some of his companions, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning:
The funerals of men and boys. So he said: The women are placed nearest to the qiblah, and the boys behind them, and the men behind that, and the Imam stands on the side nearest to the men.

key_terms.الرِّجَالُ: the men whose funeral bodies are placed after the boys
key_terms.الصِّبْيَانُ: the boys whose funeral bodies are placed after the women
key_terms.النِّسَاءُ: the women whose funeral bodies are to be placed first toward the qiblah
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader who stands nearest to the men
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of prayer, used here as the reference point for arrangement
key_terms.جَنَائِزِ: funeral biers or funeral bodies being arranged for prayer

ai.seo_question: How should men, women, and boys be arranged in funeral prayer when their جنازة are gathered together?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the arrangement of multiple جنازة bodies when women, boys, and men are gathered together for funeral prayer. It specifies their order relative to the qiblah and where the Imam should stand.
